core_obligations: Choose a closed point in a fibre (proof lines 1421-1432): take a nonempty open affine V of the integral target with generic point eta; the fibre over eta is a nonempty quasi-compact sober algebraic space, so it has a closed point x; let X' be the reduced induced closed subspace structure on the closure of x.

Properties of the restriction (proof lines 1432-1438): the restriction of the morphism to X' is surjective because its image contains the generic point, and it is proper as a composition of a closed immersion with a proper morphism; the fibre of the restriction over eta has a single point, seen by comparing the descriptions of the fibres of the two morphisms at eta.

Conclude that it is an alteration (proof lines 1438-1444): the target is decent and the restriction is separated, so the source is decent; hence the restriction is proper, surjective and generically finite, which by the characterization of alterations is exactly an alteration.
proof_roadmap: Pick a closed point of the fibre over the generic point of a nonempty open affine of the target.
Take the reduced structure on its closure and check surjectivity, properness and singleton fibre over the generic point.
Use decency of the source and the characterization of alterations to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a proper surjective morphism of algebraic spaces over an integral target there is an integral closed subspace whose restriction to the target is an alteration (statement lines 1413-1419). The proof (proof lines 1421-1446) picks a closed point of the fibre over the generic point, takes the reduced structure on its closure, verifies surjectivity, properness and the singleton fibre over the generic point, and concludes by the characterization of alterations together with the inheritance of decency. H2: a three-step construction with four inputs, written out in full.
